title: Artifact repository creation on the server: use _get_artifact_repository_for_uri for stored locations and rely on the registry marker check, not bare get_artifact_repository, so server jobs and handlers share one host policy
answers: I added a new handler that reads a stored artifact location; how do I make sure it respects the server host restriction?
Why does a server job that logs artifacts to an ftp location fail with a host-policy error while the same code works on a client?
Where is the registry-level enforcement that covers runs:/ and models:/ URIs in server processes?
body:
Path: Repository construction for artifact URIs in the tracking server: handlers in mlflow/server/handlers.py (run artifacts via _get_artifact_repo, model version and logged model artifact handlers, presigned upload, trace repo and UI log-artifact paths) and ArtifactRepositoryRegistry.get_artifact_repository in mlflow/store/artifact/artifact_repository_registry.py, which is also used inside huey jobs and job subprocesses.
Rule: Stored locations must be built with mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_artifact_repository_for_uri, which calls validate_artifact_uri_host before get_artifact_repository. The registry calls enforce_server_artifact_uri_host_policy in ArtifactRepositoryRegistry.get_artifact_repository, which is a no-op unless the _MLFLOW_SERVER_ARTIFACT_ROOT marker is in the environment, so server processes and jobs (which inherit it) are checked while clients are not. The duplicated marker names in host_policy.py must equal mlflow/server/constants.py ARTIFACT_ROOT_ENV_VAR and ARTIFACTS_DESTINATION_ENV_VAR; a test pins them. Also, _get_artifact_repo no longer carries @catch_mlflow_exception: it is an internal helper and every caller is a decorated handler, so its exceptions must propagate rather than becoming a Response.
Symptom: Server-side jobs (for example one that logs artifacts through the tracking client, or a runs:/ or models:/ URI) could still connect to a foreign host because only the HTTP handler path was guarded.
Constraints: The registry check only fires when the marker is set, so a WSGI app run without the mlflow server CLI must export the same env vars to get registry-level enforcement; the handler-level check still applies there. Renaming the marker constant without updating host_policy.py silently disables registry enforcement.
applies: Any new server-side code that resolves or builds an artifact repository from a stored or client-supplied URI in the tracking server or its jobs.
says: Background server jobs fail when logging artifacts to an external file server.
Artifact logging works from the client but fails inside server background tasks.
Server background jobs bypass host restrictions when resolving run or model artifact locations.
Enforce consistent remote storage host security across all server handlers and background workers.
search: Server-side artifact repository construction must use mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_artifact_repository_for_uri and ArtifactRepositoryRegistry.get_artifact_repository to enforce host policies across both handlers and server jobs. The registry calls enforce_server_artifact_uri_host_policy only when the _MLFLOW_SERVER_ARTIFACT_ROOT environment marker is present, ensuring server processes and job subprocesses are restricted while client processes are exempt. Applies to resolving stored or client-supplied URIs in tracking server handlers, Huey jobs, and job subprocesses, but WSGI apps running without the CLI must explicitly export marker environment variables to enable registry-level enforcement.
